cards.apply_when: the brief has gaps that would change a rule, and the person is available to answer
cards.output: at most three questions asked one at a time, and every other gap recorded as an assumption with its rationale and alternatives

cards.apply_when: verifying that tests written or helped by an AI would really catch a defect, once the implementation is green
cards.output: a mutation score for the changed production files, the surviving mutants, and an example added for every survivor that matters

cards.apply_when: the draft rules and examples are ready and before the person is asked to approve them
cards.output: a short list of how this feature could fail in the real world, each marked blocking, tracked or noise, with a rule or example added for every blocking one

cards.apply_when: a feature request has just arrived, in the person's own words, before any rule is written
cards.output: the literal ask, the job behind it, must-haves and nice-to-haves, a problem statement with goals and non-goals, and a list of gaps

cards.apply_when: a scenario failed intermittently, or before declaring a feature done when it touches time, concurrency, the network or a UI
cards.output: results of several runs on the same commit, shuffled and isolated, with each unstable scenario classified as product, test, environment or data

cards.apply_when: a request carries more than a handful of rules, several kinds of users, or more than one independent outcome
cards.output: thin vertical slices, each with its own rules and examples, in the order they should be built

cards.apply_when: writing the Given steps and drivers that create the records, files and clock a scenario depends on
cards.output: data that each scenario creates for itself, with factories, fixed seeds and no personal data

cards.apply_when: a rule has a threshold, limit, range, cut-off time or size, or a count that changes behaviour
cards.output: for every boundary, one example just outside, on, and just inside each edge

cards.apply_when: the outcome depends on a combination of several conditions, such as eligibility, pricing tiers or approval rules
cards.output: a table of every combination of conditions with its outcome, and one example per row that matters

cards.apply_when: an input can take many values that the rule treats in a few distinct ways
cards.output: one example per class of input, valid and invalid, each with a reason it is its own class

cards.apply_when: always, for every rule that takes input or depends on who is asking or on the state of the system
cards.output: for each rule, at least one example of it being refused or failing safely, or a written reason why none exists

cards.apply_when: many independent inputs each with several values, where trying every combination is too many and the rule does not link them
cards.output: a small set of examples in which every pair of values from two different inputs appears at least once

cards.apply_when: something has a lifecycle with states and events, such as orders, subscriptions, tickets or approvals
cards.output: the allowed transitions as a table, an example per transition, and an example per forbidden transition
